title: Right-derived units compare cone-quotient triangles on injective rows
statement:
Let $\mathcal A,\mathcal B$ be abelian categories [def-sp-abelian], with enough injectives in $\mathcal A$ [def-sp-injective-resolutions], and let $T:\mathcal A\to\mathcal B$ be additive [def-sp-left-exact-additive]. Use the bounded-below derived categories and the shift/cone convention of [def-weil-pbc-bounded-derived-subcategories, def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Write $\alpha_L:Q(TL)\to RT(QL)$ for the right-derived unit [lem-weil-pbc-right-derived-plus-injective]. Suppose
$$0\to E\xrightarrow{u}F\xrightarrow{v}G\to0$$
is a degreewise short exact row of bounded-below complexes of injectives of $\mathcal A$, and its termwise image under $T$ is also degreewise short exact. Put $P=\operatorname{Cone}(u)$, with $P^n=F^n\oplus E^{n+1}$ and $d(b,a)=(db+u(a),-da)$, and put $q:P\to G$, $q(b,a)=v(b)$. The complex $P$ is bounded below and termwise injective. There is a canonical complex isomorphism $\chi:T(P)\xrightarrow{\sim}\operatorname{Cone}(T(u))$ preserving the cone inclusion and negative projection, including the comparison $T(E[1])\cong T(E)[1]$. Both $q$ and $q_T:\operatorname{Cone}(T(u))\to T(G)$ are quasi-isomorphisms, and $q_T\chi=T(q)$. The invertible units $\alpha_E,\alpha_F,\alpha_G$ identify the entire image under $RT$ of
$$QE\xrightarrow{Qu}QF\xrightarrow{Qv}QG\xrightarrow{(-\operatorname{pr}_E)q^{-1}}QE[1]$$
with the distinguished triangle of the $T$-image row. More precisely, $(\alpha_E^{-1},\alpha_F^{-1},\alpha_G^{-1})$ is an isomorphism of triangles from this image to that row's triangle; its last-arrow square uses the canonical shift comparison of $RT$. Under $\alpha_P$ and $Q\chi$, $RT(Qq)$ is $Qq_T$, so its third arrow is exactly $(-\operatorname{pr}_{T(E)})q_T^{-1}$. This comparison is natural in morphisms of such short exact rows. On cones the map associated to a row morphism $(e,f,g)$ is $(b,a)\mapsto(fb,ea)$ and commutes with quotient and negative projection.

proof.text: Choose a common strict lower bound N for E,F,G. Then P^n=0 for n<N-1. For any monomorphism M→L, a map M→F^n⊕E^{n+1} has two components, each of which extends to L by injectivity; pairing the extensions proves injectivity of P^n. Thus P, as well as E,F,G, is a bounded-below complex of injectives. This argument uses only the defining extension property, not preservation of injectives by T.

Additivity gives the canonical biproduct comparison χ^n:T(F^n⊕E^{n+1})≅T(F^n)⊕T(E^{n+1}). In these coordinates the image differential has matrix ((T(d_F),T(u)),(0,-T(d_E))), so χ is a complex isomorphism. The termwise identification s_E:T(E[1])≅T(E)[1] is a chain isomorphism since T(-d_E)=-T(d_E). Matrix projection and inclusion give χ T(i)=i_T and (-pr_{T(E)})χ=s_E T(-pr_E). Likewise q_Tχ=T(v pr_F)=T(q), by their two biproduct components. These are equations of chain maps; element notation is only shorthand for biproduct components.

proof.text: Apply lem-pc-cone-short-exact-quasi-iso first to E→F→G in A and then to T(E)→T(F)→T(G) in B; the second application uses the assumed exactness of that image row. Hence q and q_T are quasi-isomorphisms, so Qq and Qq_T are invertible. By the definition of distinguished triangles, localizing the cone triangle gives a distinguished triangle. Replace its cone vertex by QG via Qq: its second arrow becomes Qv since qi=v, and its last arrow becomes δ=Q(-pr_E)(Qq)^{-1}. The identical argument in B gives δ_T=Q(-pr_{T(E)})(Qq_T)^{-1}. All complexes used are bounded below, so these are triangles in D⁺.

proof.text: Put c_L=α_L^{-1} for L=E,F,G,P. These inverses exist by lem-weil-pbc-right-derived-plus-injective and Step 1. Naturality of α gives c_M RT(Qh)=Q(T h)c_L for each chain map h:L→M between these complexes. Taking h=u,v proves the first two triangle squares. Taking h=q gives c_G RT(Qq)=Q(Tq) c_P=Qq_T Qχ c_P, using q_Tχ=T(q) from Step 2; hence RT(Qq)=c_G^{-1} Qq_T (Qχ c_P), which is precisely the claimed identification of RT(Qq) under α_P and Qχ. No assertion that T preserves all quasi-isomorphisms is needed.

proof.text: Apply lem-sc-p1-right-derived-injective-boundary with A,B,v=T and H=(E→F→G). Its hypotheses are exactly enough injectives in A, additivity of T, bounded-below termwise injectivity of the three complexes, and short exactness of the row and its T-image. The canonical boundaries are δ and δ_T of Step 3: both use the localized cone quotient and the negative projection convention. The lemma says c_E[1] σ_E RT(δ)=δ_T c_G, with the canonical shift comparison σ_E:RT(QE[1])≅RT(QE)[1]. This is the last triangle square. Together with Step 4 and the invertibility of c_E,c_F,c_G it gives the asserted isomorphism of triangles, and hence distinguishedness of the image triangle.

source.place: Tag 0152, canonical SES boundary; Tag 05TH, injective comparison; existing inverse-unit boundary theorem

proof.text: For a strict row morphism (e,f,g), the diagonal cone map C(b,a)=(fb,ea) commutes with differentials because fu=u′e. Its two components give q′C=gq and (-pr_{E′})C=e[1](-pr_E). After localization, invert the q maps to obtain δ′Qg=Qe[1]δ. The same computation applies to the T-image row; the biproduct comparison χ is natural since each of its two projections is T of the original projection. Finally naturality of α at e,f,g makes the componentwise triangle isomorphisms natural. Thus the cone comparison, quotient identification and all three triangle squares commute with row morphisms.
